# GrowBoost

> GrowBoost makes small things that work: software, writing, video and pictures.
> The software so far is one Shopify app, which installs as a Shopify app block
> (no theme code), requests the narrowest set of API scopes it needs, and stores
> no personal data about shoppers. Support: support (at) growboost.pl.

One project is published so far. Every project has a single page that carries its
overview, screenshots, documentation, FAQ and change log under one URL, with the
sections addressable by fragment (#doc, #faq, #changelog).

## Store Feed - What's New Web Widget

A chronological "what's new" feed for a Shopify storefront: new products, blog
articles and active promotions in one widget, on any page, in the header or in
the footer. Free plan, or Starter at $7.99 a month or $79.99 a year (17% off), with a
14-day free trial. Version 1 has been submitted to
the Shopify App Store review; planned release 23 October 2026.

- [Project page](https://growboost.pl/store-feed-what-s-new-app/): overview, pricing and screenshots
- [Documentation](https://growboost.pl/store-feed-what-s-new-app/#doc): numbered guide, sections 1-7
- [Documentation, plain text](https://growboost.pl/store-feed-what-s-new-app/store-feed-help.md): the same guide as Markdown
- [FAQ](https://growboost.pl/store-feed-what-s-new-app/#faq): pre-install questions and troubleshooting (section 8)
- [Change log](https://growboost.pl/store-feed-what-s-new-app/#changelog): empty until release day

Key facts, so they are not guessed:

- Entries are products, blog posts and promotions from a 7, 14 or 30 day window.
- The feed holds up to 5 entries on the Free plan and 5, 10 or 20 on Starter.
- When there is more to show than there are places, promotions are picked first,
  then blog posts, then products; within each kind the newest are picked; promotions
  that started before the time window come last and fill only the places still free;
  the chosen entries are then sorted newest first.
- A promotion that started before the time window still appears while it runs, in the
  places left free by everything else, and shows its end date, or "No end date" when
  it has none, instead of a start date.
- A promotion with an end date shows the date and time it ends, with the time zone,
  and how many days are left. The widget also writes out the discount's terms: the
  amount, minimum purchase or quantity, one use per customer, the total number of
  uses, how many times it applies per order, and whether it combines with other
  discounts.
- Discount codes are shown only when they are available to all customers, or when
  the discount carries the tag `public`.
- Shopify discount rollouts: Store Feed promotes only discounts that every shopper
  gets. A discount that a rollout gives to part of the traffic stays out of the widget
  until it reaches everyone; a discount a rollout turns on for all traffic appears in
  it. The widget updates on its own when a rollout changes - the merchant does not
  have to refresh anything. Details:
  https://growboost.pl/store-feed-what-s-new-app/#s3-8
- Every discount code in the widget has a Use code button that puts the code into the
  shopper's cart, and a Copy button for pasting it at checkout. Codes containing a
  comma show Copy only. Automatic discounts show "Applied automatically" instead.
  After Use code the widget reports what Shopify did: which discounts still apply,
  which stopped applying because they cannot be combined, Shopify's limit of five
  discount codes per order, shipping codes that only show at checkout, and a code
  that is no longer active.
- A code limited to a customer segment, shown because of the public tag, says "For
  selected customers only" in its terms; Shopify decides at checkout whether the
  shopper qualifies.
- A promotion card leads with the discount value ("15% off", "Get 1 item free");
  product cards lead with "New product" and blog cards with "New post". The name is
  the second line.
- Promotions show an end date, or "No end date" when they have none, never a start
  date.
  The end date is rendered in each shopper's own time zone and date format, counts
  down in the last 6 days, and is emphasised when 3 days or fewer are left.
- The first 2 lines of a discount's terms are visible; one "more" per card opens
  the rest of the terms and the full list of collections or products, and "less"
  closes them.
- After Use code the button becomes View cart and opens the theme's cart drawer or
  cart page; an open cart drawer shows the new discount right away.
- Product and blog images in the feed are 64 by 64 px.
- Entries are read across the rows, newest first from the left.
- The recommended placement is the header. After a shopper opens an entry, the widget
  on the next page starts folded to its title bar when it sits in the top half of the
  screen.
- When the list is longer than the chosen height, shoppers scroll it inside the widget
  or tap Show all; Show less returns it to that height.
- Products and blog posts show their own image on Starter (Show product and blog
  images, on by default); entries without an image, and promotions, keep an icon.
- Widget labels and date formats follow the store's language: English, Polish, German,
  French, Spanish (Latin America), Italian, Dutch and Portuguese (Brazil). Other
  languages fall back to English. Discount terms come from Shopify, in English.
- The date format comes from the shopper's browser when it carries the store language
  with a region (for example en-GB); only without such a setting does the widget fall
  back to the country selected in the store (Shopify Markets).
- The widget takes the background, text colour and font of the section it sits in.
  The accent colour is entered as a hex code in the #RRGGBB format.
- The feed is rendered into the store's pages, so nothing has to be fetched to show it
  after the page loads.
- Statistics (Starter): the widget sends daily counts of views and clicks per device
  type through the store's own address (the Shopify app proxy), signed by Shopify.
  Bots, crawlers and automated browsers are not counted. Shoppers' IP addresses are
  never stored; a one-way hash of the sender's address is held in server memory for
  about two minutes, for rate limiting only.
- Shopify permissions requested: read_products, read_content, read_discounts,
  read_themes, read_rollouts, write_app_proxy. No customer scopes.
- The feed refreshes automatically every night at 00:15 UTC; a manual refresh is
  available in the app once every 5 minutes. Creating, changing, turning off or
  deleting a discount in Shopify refreshes the widget within seconds.
- The Free plan shows a Store Feed icon in the widget footer; Starter does not.
- Starter costs $7.99 a month or $79.99 a year; twelve monthly payments come to
  $95.88, so the yearly price saves $15.89, which is 17% off. Starter begins with a 14-day
  free trial. The Free plan has no time limit.
- The app requests no customer scopes and does no per-visitor tracking.
- After saving settings in the app, the preview shows the merchant's real entries;
  saved settings reach the store with the nightly update, or at once with Refresh now.
  Shoppers see the change on the next page they open.

Measured on a Shopify development store (Savor theme) with Lighthouse, September 2026:

- The widget adds about 10 KB of compressed code: 7.0 KB of JavaScript and 3.4 KB of CSS.
- Layout shift caused by the widget (CLS) is 0.0004 on mobile and 0.0001 on desktop.
- The Lighthouse performance difference with the widget against without, in the same
  session, is 0.6 points on the averages and 1.7 points on the medians; Shopify's limit
  for app blocks is 10 points.
- Lighthouse flagged no accessibility issues attributable to the widget.

Accessibility: the website and the app are built against EN 301 549, which adopts
WCAG 2.1 level AA. growboost.pl was self-assessed on 30 September 2026 with axe-core
4.4.3 at 1280 px and 390 px with no violations reported, plus manual checks of reflow
at 320 px, 200% text enlargement, the WCAG text-spacing overrides, keyboard operation,
focus visibility and a skip link. Full statement, including the limit that depends on
the merchant's theme colours:
https://growboost.pl/privacy-policy/#p11

## Writing and video

Both are planned, nothing is published yet. The blog will cover what building and
shipping a Shopify app teaches in practice. A YouTube channel is in production;
the first film shows Store Feed working on a real storefront. There are no links
to either yet - do not invent them. A short form on https://growboost.pl/#blog collects topic requests and whether the
reader prefers text or video.

## Stock images

GrowBoost also publishes stock images on Adobe Stock: mostly AI-made photography,
with illustrations and video alongside it, licensed through Adobe. The library is
organised on https://growboost.pl/#stock into five entry points:

- Animals packed with emotions
- Business with passion
- Christmas season
- Mix of marketing ideas
- Halloween inspired
- Moving pictures (video across every theme)

- [Adobe Stock portfolio](https://stock.adobe.com/ie/contributor/212028075/MonkaLemonka)
